registered: 2026-11-25, before the underfloor model was run on this body. DISCLOSURE: the measured curves were read before this file was written (to find the inputs), and they are only in figures: the values below were read off Fig. 2a by eye and carry about +-0.05 in CL. The nose's underside shape is not dimensioned; it is taken from Fig. 1b as a quarter ellipse 2.5 d long and 1.03 d high.

source.reference: Ruhrmann & Zhang, Influence of Diffuser Angle on a Bluff Body in Ground Effect, J. Fluids Eng. 125 (2003) 332-338; geometry also from Zhang, Senior & Ruhrmann, Int. J. Heat Fluid Flow 25 (2004) 1-9, Fig. 1
source.tunnel: Southampton 2.1 m x 1.5 m closed circuit, moving ground, 30 m/s, load cells; CL = downforce / (q A), A the frontal area

mapping: underfloor._solve_channel (the same equations as underfloor.solve on an STL) on the gap under the body: nose relief, flat floor from 2.5 d, then the ramp at the diffuser angle from 4.95 d to 8.38 d; duct width 2 d; default discharge coefficient; reference area the frontal area (2.06 d x 2 d less the 0.35 d corner radii). The model is the floor only: it has no upper-body lift
graded: the 5 and 10 deg diffusers at h/d 0.10, 0.20 and 0.30 (attached or nearly attached flow, no hysteresis). The 15 and 20 deg diffusers separate and are reported, not graded.

registered_2.registered: 2026-11-25, after the first run failed and before the new model below was run on this body. Not blind: the measured curves (and the centreline and base pressures, Figs. 6 and 8) had been read.
registered_2.model: underfloor.solve_leaky (new). Quasi-1D with the floor's open sides: air enters (or leaves) through each open side of the gap at the local pressure difference, as a sharp-edged slot, dQ/dx = 2 g Cd U sqrt(|Cp|) with Cd = 0.61 (the textbook sharp-edged orifice); total pressure conserved along the floor (Bernoulli); no side flow where side plates close the duct (the ramp here); pressure recovery in the diffuser at effectiveness 0.80 (the existing model's constant); the exit pressure set to the measured base pressure, Cp_b = -0.25 (Fig. 8, the middle of the 5 and 20 deg diffusers' range); the inlet flow found by shooting to that exit pressure. Floor force only (no upper-body lift). No constant is fitted to the downforce data.
registered_2.graded: as registered: 5 and 10 deg diffusers at h/d 0.10, 0.20, 0.30 within 30 %

registered_3.registered: 2026-11-25, after registered_2 failed (the open-sided model with textbook constants read 2.6 to 12 times the measured downforce) and before this test was run.
registered_3.test: the same model with the diffuser effectiveness eta fitted by least squares on the 5 deg diffuser's three points only, then the 10 deg diffuser's three points predicted with that eta. Graded: the three held-out 10 deg points within 30 %. Also reported, not graded: 15 and 20 deg with the same eta.

note_after_reruns: registered_2 and registered_3 both failed. The open-sided model was then moved out of suspension/aero/underfloor.py into scripts/underbody_diffuser_benchmark.py (solve_leaky), unchanged, so the reruns stay reproducible without shipping a model that failed.

registered_4_ranking.registered: 2026-11-25, after the three absolute-value misses and before this test was computed. Not blind: both the measured values and the model's values had been seen, and the model looked to order them right; this registration says so.
registered_4_ranking.why: KinematiK is a prevalidation tool: its floor model is for ranking designs before CFD or a tunnel, so the claim to test is the order of downforce across designs, not its size
registered_4_ranking.test: the shipped underfloor model (first-run mapping, unchanged), all nine measured points: every pair of points; a pair whose measured CL differ by 0.05 or less (the reading uncertainty) is a tie and is left out; the model must put at least 90 % of the remaining pairs in the measured order
